claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 1034 (fetched today): "Name servers are the repositories of information that make up the domain database"; the document describes DNS as using "domain names to identify hosts; queries for address resources return Internet host addresses." That is "turns a name into an IP address by asking machines whose job is to hold the answer". Caveat: versions.yaml pins no `standards` entry for DNS, so this comes from rfc-editor.org, the publisher already pinned for http/tls/jwt (see the version issue).

RFC 1034 s5.3.1: "All that the remaining stub needs is a list of name server addresses that will perform the recursive requests. This type of resolver presumably needs the information in a configuration file." The "handed to it by the network" half is execution, run today: `docker exec donhang-lab cat /etc/resolv.conf` prints "# Generated by Docker Engine." and "nameserver 127.0.0.11", written when the container joined network `donhang`. The lesson hedges with "usually", which no pinned source quantifies.

RFC 1034: "In existing systems, hosts and other resources often have several names that identify the same resource", and on host-name-to-address translation "a multiple address return is recommended" — one name, several addresses. Execution confirms the other half in the lab: /etc/hosts on donhang-lab holds `172.28.0.12 donhang-lab` while `nslookup lab` answers `172.28.0.12`. The claim is scoped to "the kind this lesson uses", so no record-type detail is asserted.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034.txt s3.6, s5.2.2; docker exec donhang-lab bash /repo/scripts/network/resolve.sh

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 1035 s3.2.1: TTL is "a 32 bit signed integer that specifies the time interval that the resource record may be cached before the source of the information should again be consulted." TTL is a field of the resource record, so "stated together with a record" is exact, and "may keep using it before asking again" restates "cached before the source of the information should again be consulted".

Settled by execution on the image the lesson ships. Throwaway container from donhang-lab:stage-0 on network `donhang` started with `--add-host db:10.99.99.99`: /etc/hosts holds `10.99.99.99 db`, `getent hosts db` answers 10.99.99.99 although the resolver holds 172.28.0.11 — the file is read first; `nslookup db` in that same container answers 172.28.0.11 — it skips the file. nslookup there is BusyBox v1.37.0 (/usr/bin/nslookup -> /bin/busybox). No hosts(5)/nsswitch page is pinned, so the ordering rests on execution.
claim_verdicts.source: docker run --rm --network donhang --add-host db:10.99.99.99 donhang-lab:stage-0 sh -c 'getent hosts db; nslookup db'

claim_verdicts.evidence: docker-compose.yml at stage-0, service `lab`: `extra_hosts: - "donhang.local:127.0.0.1"` — the lab's own configuration writes the line. Runtime: the script's last line prints `127.0.0.1\tdonhang.local` in /etc/hosts on donhang-lab. STAGE.md at stage-0: "add `127.0.0.1 donhang.local` to your hosts file to open it in a browser" (of https://donhang.local:8443). The same line the lesson names.
claim_verdicts.source: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-0:docker-compose.yml, stage-0:STAGE.md; docker exec donhang-lab bash /repo/scripts/network/resolve.sh

claim_verdicts.evidence: Docker docs mirror, engine/network/_index.md L262-266: "Containers that attach to a custom network use Docker's embedded DNS server. ... The embedded DNS server address is `127.0.0.11`." Runtime: resolv.conf on donhang-lab holds `nameserver 127.0.0.11`; `nslookup db` prints `Server: 127.0.0.11` then `Address: 172.28.0.11`, `nslookup lab` prints `172.28.0.12`; both addresses pinned by `ipv4_address` in docker-compose.yml at stage-0. "Run by the lab itself" simplifies "run by the container platform for this lab's network" — loose about who runs it, not false about where it lives.

RFC 1034 on redundancy: "A given zone will be available from several name servers to insure its availability in spite of host or communication link failure. By administrative fiat, we require every zone to be available on at least two servers." On where the answer changes: "all data originates in master files scattered through the hosts that use the domain system. These master files are updated by local system administrators." The RFC speaks of zones where the lesson says names — a simplification, not an error.

RFC 1034: "The TTL describes how long a RR can be cached before it should be discarded." RFC 1035 s3.2.1: the TTL is "the time interval that the resource record may be cached before the source of the information should again be consulted." Keeping an answer for its TTL and serving it to later askers without asking again is exactly what those sentences permit, and it is what makes a served answer older than the moment it is served.

Execution today: `docker exec donhang-lab nslookup db` prints `Server:\t127.0.0.11` / `Address:\t127.0.0.11:53` then `Name:\tdb` / `Address: 172.28.0.11` — it names the resolver it asked and prints what came back. Running the whole script (`bash /repo/scripts/network/resolve.sh | cat -A`) reproduces outputs/stage-0/scripts/network/resolve.txt and the lesson's output block byte for byte, tabs included.

Execution: /etc/hosts on donhang-lab contains `127.0.0.1\tdonhang.local`, yet `nslookup donhang.local` prints `Server: 127.0.0.11` / `Address: 127.0.0.11:53` then `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached` — it asked the resolver, never read the file, and that resolver has no answer for the name; `getent hosts donhang.local` on the same box answers `127.0.0.1 donhang.local` from the file. Both halves confirmed.
claim_verdicts.source: docker exec donhang-lab sh -c 'nslookup donhang.local; getent hosts donhang.local'

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live /etc/hosts printed by the script today: `127.0.0.1 localhost`; `::1 localhost ip6-localhost ip6-loopback`; `fe00:: ip6-localnet`; `ff00:: ip6-mcastprefix`; `ff02::1 ip6-allnodes`; `ff02::2 ip6-allrouters`; `127.0.0.1 donhang.local`; `172.28.0.12 donhang-lab` — four further fixed names beyond the localhost line, as claimed. Neither `db` nor `lab` appears, and nslookup's `Server:` line shows both were answered by 127.0.0.11.

Execution: the script's third question prints `** server can't find no-such-host.donhang: NXDOMAIN`, matching the captured output at stage-0. RFC 1035 s4.1.1, RCODE 3: "Name Error - Meaningful only for responses from an authoritative name server, this code signifies that the domain name referenced in the query does not exist." The lesson attributes the report to "a resolver", which is who relays it here (127.0.0.11).

RFC 1035 s4.1.1 RCODE 3: the domain name "does not exist" — the failure comes from the name system, and the run prints no address, so nothing could be dialled. The other outcome is the previous lesson's script scripts/network/who-listens.sh, whose loop tries `localhost:9999` with `nc -z` and whose captured run reports `localhost:9999 is closed`: the box was found and nothing was listening. Two layers, two failures, as the claim states.

Live /etc/hosts on donhang-lab ends `172.28.0.12\tdonhang-lab`, and the same run's `nslookup lab` prints `Name:\tlab` / `Address: 172.28.0.12`. docker-compose.yml at stage-0 gives service `lab` `hostname: donhang-lab` and `ipv4_address: 172.28.0.12`. One address, two names, exactly as section 5 states.
claim_verdicts.source: docker exec donhang-lab bash /repo/scripts/network/resolve.sh; git -C examples/don-hang show stage-0:docker-compose.yml

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 1034 on cache handling: implementations "convert the interval specified in arriving RRs to some sort of absolute time when the RR is stored in the cache", and "the TTL describes how long a RR can be cached before it should be discarded". The clock therefore starts when that server stored the answer, not when the zone's owner changed it; servers store at different moments, so they stop serving the old answer at different moments.

Execution both ways on one network: `docker exec donhang-lab getent hosts donhang.local` answers `127.0.0.1` from the file, while `docker exec donhang-db getent hosts donhang.local` prints nothing — the name is absent from that container's /etc/hosts. Docker docs, engine/network/_index.md, "Custom hosts": "Custom hosts, defined in `/etc/hosts` on the host machine, aren't inherited by containers." Same network, same resolver, one machine resolves the name and the other does not.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/docker-docs/content/manuals/engine/network/_index.md (Custom hosts); docker exec donhang-db getent hosts donhang.local

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 1034 on recursive service: "In recursive mode the name server acts in the role of a resolver and returns either an error or the answer, but never referrals" — that is asking on the asker's behalf and passing the answer back. On the chain: "The response contains an error, the answer, or a referral to some other server 'closer' to the answer", which the resolver then follows. Both halves supported.

The live run prints eight /etc/hosts lines; five of them (`::1`, `fe00::`, `ff00::`, `ff02::1`, `ff02::2`) write the address in the second notation and three (`127.0.0.1 localhost`, `127.0.0.1 donhang.local`, `172.28.0.12 donhang-lab`) in the first. The lesson's output block is identical line for line, so "Five of its lines" is correct as printed.
claim_verdicts.source: docker exec donhang-lab bash /repo/scripts/network/resolve.sh | cat -A; examples/don-hang outputs/stage-0/scripts/network/resolve.txt
